evidence: Abstract and Secs.3-5 (HTML full text): LIME stability (VSI/CSI over repeated calls) for quantum SVMs and quantum neural networks on tabular UCI datasets
problem: Whether LIME explanations of quantum classifiers are stable enough to be trusted in critical domains.
method: Quantum SVM and quantum neural network classifiers (Qiskit), ideal and noisy simulation; LIME tabular explainer; repeated LIME calls per instance; Visani et al.'s VSI and CSI indices.
data: Tabular classification datasets from critical domains (UCI repository).
evaluation: Variables Stability Index and Coefficients Stability Index (0-100) across repeated applications.
findings: LIME gave explanations for quantum SVMs and QNNs that were interpretable and stable in both ideal and noisy quantum settings (abstract).
limitations: Ours: simulated quantum hardware; run-to-run stability only.
repro: Uses public lime and lime_stability code and Qiskit; datasets public.
qa_notes: Q4 no competing explainer; Q7 brief; Q10 repeated LIME calls.

evidence: Abstract, Secs.2-3 (pp.1-11): SHAP rank stability under station-level bootstrap, predictor perturbation and model class in a reliability performance index (tabular lagged-predictor data)
read_from: Publisher PDF (Machine Learning: Science and Technology 7(4):045033, open access)
problem: Highly ranked SHAP predictors are not necessarily reliable explanations across spatial, resampling, model and predictor-correlation uncertainty.
method: Station-held-out validation of tree models; SHAP importance; station-level bootstrap refits; rank stability (Spearman, top-10 overlap), directional consistency, ablation and multi-model comparison combined into an RPI; controlled grouped benchmark.
data: Daily discharge at 51 USGS stations in the Chesapeake Bay watershed, 1990-2024, with time-safe lagged climate-mode predictors (station-season rows) (p.5).
evaluation: Within-model rank, Spearman correlation, top-10 overlap; bootstrap CIs (pp.9-11).
findings: RPI recovered the predefined stable drivers more accurately than raw SHAP importance in the benchmark; September PDO was the most spatially transferable and explanation-stable predictor (pp.1,22).
limitations: Authors: no local meteorological predictors; RPI does not establish causality (p.22).
repro: Supplementary material online; no code link found.
qa_notes: Q8 supplement only; Q10 bootstrap replicates.

evidence: Abstract, Secs.3-7 (pp.1-10): SHAP stability under shuffling, missingness and Gaussian noise at four levels on four tabular datasets
read_from: Zenodo preprint of the DSAA 2023 paper (doi 10.1109/DSAA60987.2023.10302535)
problem: Measures of explanation quality are lacking; how stable are SHAP explanations under data perturbation?
method: Random forest; three perturbation types (feature shuffling, missing values, Gaussian noise) at four strengths; SHAP values from models trained on clean data and applied to perturbed data; correlation and error measures; Shapiro-Wilk then paired t-test or Wilcoxon.
data: Breast Cancer, Iris, Wine and CIC-IDS2018 (p.2).
evaluation: Correlation and error between clean and perturbed SHAP values; statistical tests of distribution equality (p.5).
findings: SHAP values changed with perturbation strength; stability varied by dataset, with CIC-IDS2018 showing the largest decreases (pp.10).
limitations: Authors: random forest only; dataset-dependence (p.10). Ours: perturbations not prediction-preserving.
qa_notes: Q4 one model; Q8 data only; Q10 seeds not reported.

evidence: Abstract and Methods (HTML full text): explanation stability reported as a separate dimension (30 repeated runs) in a five-dimension trustworthiness framework on tabular METABRIC (borderline)
read_from: Publisher HTML (Future Business Journal 12(1):305, 2026, open access)
problem: Clinical AI decision support is judged mainly on predictive metrics, not on explanation stability and related properties.
method: Decision tree, SVM and XGBoost; 30 independent runs; five dimensions: predictive reliability (ROC-AUC), explainability (SHAP-LIME agreement), explanation stability, clinical plausibility, imbalance robustness (G-mean).
data: METABRIC HER2 status (1,980 cases: 1,733 negative, 247 positive).
evaluation: Mean pairwise top-10 feature-set overlap across 100 LIME explanations of evaluation instances per model and experimental repetition; reported across 30 repeated holdout evaluations alongside the other trustworthiness dimensions.
findings: XGBoost had the highest ROC-AUC (0.983) and explanation stability (0.652 +/- 0.045) (abstract).
limitations: Authors: single retrospective dataset; no external or prospective validation.
repro: Public Kaggle dataset; no code link found.
qa_notes: Q5 separate top-10 LIME feature-overlap measure; comparisons span evaluation instances rather than necessarily repeated calls for one fixed instance, so interpretation as local stability needs caution; Q6 single case study; Q8 no code link found; Q9 clinical data, ethics brief; Q10 30 runs.

evidence: Abstract and Sec.4 (HTML full text): retraining stability of SHAP rankings (seeds 42-44) within an XAI reliability audit on tabular UNSW-NB15 and IoT-ToN (borderline)
read_from: Publisher HTML (J. Computer Virology and Hacking Techniques 22(1):80, 2026, open access)
problem: High IDS detection performance does not show whether explanations are reliable.
method: XGBoost, logistic regression, random forest; SHAP vs permutation importance agreement; sufficiency/comprehensiveness retraining tests; retraining-stability analysis over three seeds; spurious-feature injection; radar profile.
evaluation: Spearman agreement; top-k faithfulness tests (k = 3, 5, 10); retraining stability.
findings: Logistic regression gave the most stable explanations but weaker detection; high performance did not imply trustworthy explanations (abstract).
limitations: Ours: only three retraining seeds; no input perturbation.
repro: Public datasets; no code link found.
qa_notes: Q7 brief; Q8 data only; Q10 three seeds only.

evidence: Abstract, Methods and Results (Europe PMC full text): AKDE-LIME stability and robustness vs LIME, KernelSHAP, TreeSHAP and Anchor across noise levels 5-20% on five tree models (tabular UCI data)
read_from: Europe PMC full text PMC13014406 (Applied Artificial Intelligence, 2026, open access)
problem: LIME explanations are unstable because different neighbourhood samples give different explanations.
method: AKDE-LIME: density-aware kernel weighting of perturbed samples combined with proximity; compared with LIME, KernelSHAP, TreeSHAP and Anchor on five tree-based models; grid of noise levels (0.05-0.20) and 10-50 evaluated instances.
data: A real-world tabular dataset from the UCI repository (Data Availability).
evaluation: Stability (rank-correlation-based score after Zhou et al.) and robustness (relative change in importance after Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola); Jaccard distance for Anchor rules.
findings: AKDE-LIME was significantly more stable and robust than LIME and reached stability comparable to TreeSHAP (e.g., decision tree 0.0011 vs 0.0158) (Results; Conclusions).
limitations: Authors: limitations section discusses scope; future work on other data. Ours: one dataset.
repro: Data openly available (UCI); no code link found.
qa_notes: Q3 single dataset; Q6 one dataset; Q8 data only; Q10 noise grid and repeated instances.

evidence: Abstract, Secs.3-4 (pp.1100-1108): ST-LIME fixed-noise sampling and Feature Sequence Stability Index vs five LIME variants on four tabular datasets
read_from: Publisher PDF (Int. J. Intelligent Engineering and Systems 17(6), 2024, open access)
problem: Randomised synthetic sampling makes LIME explanations unstable.
method: ST-LIME: fixed-noise synthetic sample generation scaled by feature standard deviations; compared with five state-of-the-art LIME variants over 10 repeated explanations per sample.
data: Parkinson's, Breast Cancer, EEG and Bank datasets (p.7).
evaluation: Feature Sequence Stability Index (FSSI) and fidelity.
findings: ST-LIME reached FSSI = 1.0 on the datasets reported and outperformed the compared techniques on average (Table 2, p.8).
limitations: Authors: extension to images and text proposed (p.9). Ours: determinism trivially yields perfect run-to-run stability.
qa_notes: Q3 dataset sizes brief; Q6 small; Q8 none; Q10 10 repeated explanations.

evidence: Abstract, Secs.3-4 (pp.1-7): CTGAN-LIME stability vs LIME on Heart Disease, Red Wine Quality and Census Income
read_from: Publisher PDF (Proc. 10th World Congress EECSS'24, paper CIST 158, open access)
problem: LIME's random neighbourhood sampling causes selection variability and class imbalance in neighbourhoods, reducing stability.
method: CTGAN-LIME: CTGAN-generated neighbourhood samples with conditional vectors for class balance, plus real samples; ridge surrogate; feedforward neural-network black box.
data: Heart Disease, Red Wine Quality and Census Income (Fig.3, p.7).
evaluation: Local fidelity, stability and local concordance vs LIME.
findings: CTGAN-LIME improved reliability and stability of explanations relative to LIME across the datasets (abstract; Fig.3).
limitations: Ours: short proceedings paper; stability metric briefly defined; no statistical tests.
qa_notes: Q2 brief; Q4 LIME only; Q5 brief; Q8 none; Q10 not detailed.

evidence: Abstract and Sec.3 (pp.1,6): 'attribution consistency' is cross-method agreement (Spearman between SHAP, LIME and permutation rankings), not stability of one explainer
Abstract, Methods (pp.113-120): SHAP ranking stability (Sequential Rank Agreement) of XGBoost/LightGBM across 64 simulated conditions and BPJS claims data
read_from: Publisher PDF via journal viewer (Jurnal Statistika dan Komputasi 5(1):113-, 2026, open access)
problem: SHAP interpretation stability may depend on data characteristics and the model used.
method: XGBoost and LightGBM fitted repeatedly with fixed hyperparameters; 64 simulated datasets varying minority-class proportion, feature correlation and number of features; SMOTE/ADASYN on empirical data; fixed seeds.
data: Simulation population of 600,000 observations; anonymised BPJS Kesehatan claims 2018-2023 (22 features), 70:30 stratified splits.
evaluation: Sequential Rank Agreement of SHAP rankings across repeated runs.
findings: Higher feature correlation and extreme class imbalance reduced ranking stability; imbalance handling improved performance and interpretation stability on BPJS data (abstract).
limitations: Ours: retraining stability only; regional health dataset.
repro: Python packages listed; no code link.
qa_notes: Q4 two models only; Q8 no code; Q9 anonymised health data; Q10 repeated fits with fixed seeds.

evidence: Abstract and Results (pp.13-19): stability of LIME interpretations between imbalanced and SMOTE-balanced nutritional-status data
read_from: Publisher PDF via journal viewer (Indonesian Journal of Infomatics 1(2), 2026, open access)
problem: Class imbalance may change LIME-based interpretations in nutritional-status prediction.
method: Random forest trained on original imbalanced data and on SMOTE-balanced data; LIME explanations compared between scenarios.
evaluation: Interpretation stability score from feature changes and contributions between scenarios.
findings: Interpretation stability score reached 0.80: fairly stable but not fully robust to changes in data distribution (abstract; results).
limitations: Ours: single comparison of two scenarios; stability score loosely defined; no repetitions or tests.
repro: No code or data link found.
qa_notes: Q4 no baseline; Q6 weak; Q8 none; Q9 child health data, ethics not discussed; Q10 no repetitions.
